British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain.
Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
• democracy • rule of law • individual liberty • mutual respect • tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs

Welcome
Headteacher's Welcome
Hello and welcome to Sir John Heron Primary School! We are a thriving two-form entry primary school with a nursery and a special resource provision for children with profound and multiple learning disabilities (PMLD). Nestled in the lively heart of Manor Park, East London, our school is proud to serve a wonderfully diverse community, enriching the educational journey for all our pupils.
At Sir John Heron, we serve a multilingual community that belong to a variety of world religions. This diversity creates a vibrant and engaging learning atmosphere that sparks interest and understanding among our pupils. We believe that for children to flourish in every aspect of life, they need to develop essential qualities like curiosity, communication, courage, and compassion. Our thoughtfully designed curriculum promotes these skills, helping our students build a strong foundation for future success, well-being, and active participation in society.
We take great pride in preparing our students not just for the next step in their educational journey, but also for life as kind, capable, and courageous global citizens. Alongside supporting our pupils, we are dedicated to working hand-in-hand with our community. We truly value the rich culture, ideas, and support that our neighbourhood brings to our school, and we aim to strengthen these connections through collaboration and shared initiatives.
As the headteacher, I am incredibly proud of our pupils and their enthusiastic approach to learning. I look forward to partner with you and the community as we continue to grow our school and enhance the learning experiences for all our students.

PE and Sport Premium
PE and Sport Premium Grant
Please read the information below which gives details of our PE and Sport Premium Grant and how we allocate the funding.
At our school, we believe every child deserves the opportunity to build a healthy, active lifestyle, develop confidence, and enjoy physical education.
PE and Sport Premium
Understanding the PE & Sport Premium
Historically, the Government provided direct annual grants to primary schools through the Primary PE and Sport Premium. As part of nationwide reforms, the Department for Education is transitioning school sports funding into a new national PE and School Sport Partnerships Network. During this multi-year transition phase, our school receives a reduced, one-off transitional funding payment.
The school carefully directs these limited transitional funds to ensure we preserve high-quality physical education, protect core sports opportunities, and build lasting staff skills.
Our 5 Key Priorities
We focus our available funding across five core areas recommended by the Department for Education:
1. Staff Training & Confidence: Upskilling our teaching team to ensure high-quality PE lessons for every year group.
2. Daily Active Habits: Keeping all children moving regularly throughout the school day.
3. Whole-School Well-Being: Using sport and movement to boost pupil health, focus, and general well-being.
4. Broad & Inclusive Experiences: Offering a diverse range of physical activities and introducing pupils to new sports.
5. Fair Competition: Giving pupils of all abilities the opportunity to take part in local school games, events, and sports competitions.

Anti-Bullying Ambassadors - Concerned about Bullying?
Bullying is:
"Lots of times and on purpose."
As upstanders:
"WE MAKE SOME NOISE"
At Sir John Heron Primary School, we have Anti-bullying Ambassadors. Children from Year 2 to 6 have been selected as our Ambassadors and have been specially trained by the Diana Award charity. The training provided them with the skills to help children if they have any issues in school or outside school including online.
The Ambassadors are easy to find in the playground as they wear blue hi-vis jackets. If you have problems or concerns, go and talk to an Anti-bullying Ambassador. They are here to help you!
Remember, if you or someone you know is being bullied, you can talk to one of the Anti-Bullying Ambassadors, put a note in the worry box or tell a trusted adult.

Wraparound Childcare Provision
We offer a Wraparound Childcare Provision for parents/carers of pupils at Sir John Heron which runs from 3.15pm-6pm on school days. For any child that requires one-to-one support due to Special Educational Needs and Disabilities, an individual assessment will need to take place to confirm whether we are able to allocate a full time place.
Wraparound Provision Charges:
£40 per week (5 days)
An afternoon meal is provided to children at the end of the school day at 3.15pm, plus children will enjoy a range of activities, including:
There are a limited number of places for the provision, however with enough notice, we may be able to accommodate adhoc childcare requests as and when needed if the provision is not at capacity.
If you are interested in a place in our Wraparound provision, please contact Mrs Khan at the Main Office on 020 8514 9860 for an application form.
For ongoing places, parents/carers will be invoiced half a term in advance. For families that claim Child-Tax Credits, our URN is 132789.

Are you worried about anything?
Worried whilst at school?
Whilst at school, if you have any worries about anything, you can speak to one of our Designated Safeguarding Leads:
Our Mental Health First Aider: Miss Werrin;
or another trusted adult.
Who else can help?
You can also contact these services for support, either online or over the phone:
Free, safe and anonymous online support where you can talk to friendly counsellors for help and advice.
Worries about the World: Some things that happen in the world can make us scared, confused, and unsafe, or like we don’t have any control. However you feel, it can really help to share your feelings and get support. You can visit the ChildLine website or call them on 0800 1111 if you have any worries, including about bullying, the news, natural disasters, politics, wars and extremism. Contact them online or on the phone, anytime. You don't even have to tell them your name.
The Diana Award Anti-Bullying Campaign Support Centre:
You will find advice / support for a variety of bullying issues.
Are you worried about something that has happened online?
Sometimes things happen online that make us feel worried, scared or upset. Whatever has happened, it's not your fault. The best thing to do is to tell an adult you trust what has happened and how you are feeling, so that they can help you.
Think of an adult you trust. It could be:
If you still feel you need help after speaking to someone, don't give up! Speak to another trusted adult. You can use some options below to help you:
Are you worried about anything you have seen online? Perhaps you have accidentally clicked on a button on an app and bought something, or someone from an online game is trying to message you. If you are worried about anything that's happened online, fill in the Online Worry Box form and an adult from school will come back to you to help you.
If you are worried about online bullying or other online concerns, don't forget that you can also get help by calling Childline on 0800 1111 or you can speak to a Childline counsellor using their online chat here.
If you need more help because of something that has happened online or in 'the real world', like if someone has tried to make you do something you don't want to do, or said something bad will happen if you don't do what they say, you can report this to CEOP by clicking the button below. Music
Subject Areas
Music
What is our aim and vision?
Music is a unique and powerful form of communication that can change the way people feel, think and act. It combines creativity with emotion, enabling personal expression, reflection and development. The National Curriculum for music aims to ensure that all children: perform, listen to, review and evaluate music; are taught to sing, create and compose music; understand and explore how music is created, produced, and communicated. At Sir John Heron Primary School, we aspire to provide our children with a rich and varied music curriculum, enabling them to gain a firm understanding of the subject. We provide the children with the skills and knowledge required of successful musicians. Children will leave Sir John Heron Primary School with an appreciation for the joy of music, a love for singing and a range of musical experiences and skills.
How are we teaching and assessing?
Music is taught exclusively by a HLTA, using the Charanga scheme of work, which ensures progression of skills throughout each year group. Children are provided with the opportunity to analyse and comprehend parts of music and gain a range of musical experiences through the exposure of different musical traditions and genres. Our music curriculum also provides children with the ability to give precise explanations, using musical terminology effectively, accurately, and appropriately. During their early years the children will encounter a curriculum rich in opportunities to explore music. The children will be encouraged to listen to music and focus on how sounds can create feelings and ideas, as well as responding to musical stimuli though dance and movements. In addition, children will also create musical sounds of their own, though playing with musical instruments with increasing control and success. As children move into KS1, they play musical instruments and sing a variety of songs from memory, adding accompaniments and creating short compositions, with increasing confidence, imagination and control. They explore and enjoy how sounds and silence can create different moods and effects. In Key Stage 2, children sing songs and play instruments with increasing confidence, skill and expression, as well as with an increasing awareness of their own contribution to a group or class performance. They improvise, and develop their own musical compositions, in response to a variety of different stimuli with increasing personal involvement, independence and creativity. Children are assessed against National Curriculum requirements for music.
What are our outcomes?
The nature of the music curriculum at Sir John Heron Primary School encourages personal traits such as achievement, self-confidence, interaction with and awareness of others, and self-reflection. Music will also develop an understanding of culture and history, both in relation to children individually, as well as ethnicities from across the world. Drawing upon the knowledge and skills developed during their time here, children will be able to enjoy music in as many ways as they choose – either as listener, creator or performer, individually or as part of a group. The music curriculum ensures that children build the confidence and skills to perform whenever opportunities may arise.

Welcome to our Music Latest Learning!
At Sir John Heron Primary School, we follow the National Curriculum for music with lessons being delivered through the Charanga scheme.
Click here to view the programme of study from the National Curriculum for music for KS1 and KS2:
Let Your Spirit Fly - Year 3 - W/B 28.09.26
This half term, the children in year 3 are learning their new song ‘Let Your Spirit Fly’. This song has a quite tricky high note in the chorus that both classes have done very well at singing. They started the term practising the ‘Friendship Song’ that they learned in year 2 - to refresh their skills in the first lesson back. They have listened to a variety of music, some songs and some instrumental, and have done very well at describing what they have heard.
Hands, Feet, Heart - Playing instruments in Year 2 - W/B 21.09.26
Year 2 have been working very hard on the song ‘Hands, Feet, Heart’ for the past couple of weeks. We have learned to play an instrumental version of the song and have been working playing in time as a whole class. We practise each song by clapping along to the music and saying the correct notes for the song at the right time. Then we move to our instruments and practise playing the notes by ourselves and the class – all without the music. After this, we add the music in and practise playing with the backtrack. In the next few weeks, we will also begin to learn to improvise – make up our own music. We always try to make the patterns of music we play as interesting as possible and not too repetitive! The song has been an enjoyable task to sing – the chorus has the girls and boys singing separately for some of the lines. So we have been practising taking turns to sing our lines.
Hey You! Learning in Year 1 - W/B 07.09.26
In year 1 this half term we began by listening to the main song that we will learn to sing which is called ‘Hey You’.The children talked about this song and described it, thinking about the speed of the song and whether it was fast or slow, the volume of the song and whether it was loud or quiet, how songs made them feel and what they heard in terms of instruments and voices. It was the first time the children in year 1 had played the xylophone so we spent some time learning how to hold the beater and hit the xylophone properly. We also did some work using the note B, which we will carry on into next week.
2025-26
Recapping Year 1 Learning - W/B 06.07.26
Year 1 have been having lots of fun in music this half term revisiting some of the songs and tunes we have played throughout the year. We played songs along with ‘Hey You’, ‘In the Groove’ as well as ‘Your Imagination’ and ‘Round and Round’. We carefully practised each tune together with the class and on our own to make sure our playing was as accurate as possible. We also enjoyed singing along to these songs as well as learning a new song to sing along with everyone at the final end of year assembly.
Xylophones in Year 4 - W/B 29.06.26
Year 4 have been revisiting some of their old songs and units this half term and using the skills we have developed on the xylophone, as well as other instruments, to see how well we have improved. We have revisited tunes such as ‘Mamma Mia’, ‘Lean on Me’ as well as ‘Blackbird’ among others. The classes also had a go at working in pairs to play two different tunes at the same time which was quite the challenge, but they did really well at it. Much fun was also had in singing those old songs using their amazing singing voices.
Xylophones in Year 2 - W/B 22.06.26
In year 2 this half term we have been spending some time testing the skills we have developed for the xylophone by looking at the different songs and tunes we have played throughout the year. We have played tunes from ‘Hands, Feet Heart’, ‘I Wanna Play in a Band’ as well as ‘Zootime’ and we have been looking at old videos of our performances of these tunes to see what we could improve for each one. We have also been practising singing an amazing song that we will be performing at our Graduation Ceremony - Reach for the Stars! It will be amazing and we hope our families can attend to celebrate and watch our performance.
Recorders in Year 6 - W/B 15.06.26
In year 6 this half term the classes are revisiting the recorder in their music lessons. In these first few weeks, they have practised the notes G, A, B and C. They have been using these notes to play along to some practise videos from youtube as well as playing along with music from songs they have covered from previous terms in year 6, such as ‘Happy’ and ‘You’ve Got a Friend’.
Revisiting Previous Learning in Year 3 - W/B 08.06.26
This half term, the children in year 3 are going back to and revisiting some of the songs and tunes that they have performed throughout the year. This first week back we focused on ‘Let Your Spirit Fly’ that they covered first in September. We sang through the song again and the children did excellently at remembering to sing the words correctly after so long. They also played along to the music using claves to help remember the rhythm and xylophones to play the melody. In further weeks, the classes will revisit other songs including ‘Three Little Birds’, ‘The Dragon Song’ and ‘Bringing Us Together’.
Revisiting Previous Learning in Year 5 - W/B 01.06.26
This half term, year 5 are going back to and revisiting some of the songs and tunes that they have performed throughout the year. This first week back we focused on ‘Livin’ on a Prayer’ that they covered first in September. We sang through the song again and the children did very well at remembering to sing the words correctly. They also played along to the music using claves to help remember the rhythm and xylophones to play the melody. In further weeks, the classes will revisit other songs including ‘Make You Feel My Love’, ‘The Fresh Prince of Bel Air’ and ‘Dancing in the Street’.
